ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “not one thought arises.” The phrase is quoted in Zhang Zhuo's verse, “not a single thought arises—the whole body appears; the six faculties barely move and clouds cover it.” Yuanwu places it beside resting, not falling into sense-objects, and not dwelling in conceptual imagining.
EvidenceBody: Yongjue gives an explicit explanation: “this mind functions yet is constantly still, is still yet constantly functions,” and says one's thoughts remain apart from encountered objects. The records also subject the phrase to public testing. the recorded questioner asks Yunmen whether not a single thought arising still has a fault; Yunmen answers “Mount Sumeru.” Xuedou later asks Zhimen why it has a fault and is struck when he comes forward.
